about.title: About BESSER
about.para1: BESSER is a low-code platform for smart software modeling and code generation. It provides a Python-based metamodel (B-UML) for describing domain models, state machines, GUI designs, agents, and more.
about.para2: The <brand>Web Modeling Editor</brand> is the online visual editor for creating and editing BESSER models, generating code, and deploying applications.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
shortcuts.description: Available keyboard shortcuts across the editor.

guide.title: How The Editor Works
guide.description: Complete modeling guide with examples and visuals.

class.label: Class Diagram
class.summary: Model classes, relationships, constraints, and advanced UML structures.

addClass.title: Add Class
addClass.body: Drag and drop a class shape from the left palette onto the modeling canvas.

addAssociation.title: Add Association Or Generalization
addAssociation.body: Select a source class, then drag from a blue connection point to another class. For multiplicities, use values like 1, 0..1, 0..*, 1..*, or 2..4.

editClass.title: Edit Class
editClass.body:
Double-click a class to edit its name, attributes, and methods.

Attribute format examples: + attribute : type, + attribute, attribute. Primitive types include int, float, str, bool, time, date, datetime, timedelta, and any.

Visibility: + public, - private, # protected. Method examples: + notify(sms: str = 'message'), - findBook(title: str): Book, validate().

editAssociation.title: Edit Association Or Generalization
editAssociation.body: Double-click a relationship to edit type (unidirectional, bidirectional, composition, generalization), name, source/target role names, and multiplicities.

deleteMove.title: Delete And Move
deleteMove.body:
Select a class and press Delete or Backspace to remove it.

Move elements by dragging them or using keyboard arrows.

Use Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y for undo/redo.

oclConstraint.title: OCL Constraint
oclConstraint.body:
Drag the OCL shape, then write constraints such as Context "ClassName" .... You can connect constraints to classes using dotted links.

Constraint syntax validation runs during Quality Check and is powered by B-OCL.

associationClass.title: Association Class
associationClass.body: Create an association class by linking a class element to an existing association center point. You can define attributes like a regular class. Note: current generators do not support association classes.

object.label: Object Diagram
object.summary: Represent concrete runtime instances and their links.

about.title: About Object Diagrams
about.body: Object diagrams show instances of classes at a specific moment in time, including current attribute values and links.

addObject.title: Add Object
addObject.body: Drag and drop an object element from the left panel to the canvas.

editObject.title: Edit Object
editObject.body:
Double-click an object to edit name, type, and attribute values.

Use naming format objectName : ClassName. For values, use attributeName = value (for example age = 25).

addLink.title: Add Object Link
addLink.body: Click an object, drag from a blue connection point, and drop on another object to create a link.

editLink.title: Edit Object Link
editLink.body: Double-click a link to update its properties such as role/name information.

deleteMove.title: Delete, Move, And Best Practices
deleteMove.body:
Delete objects/links with Delete or Backspace. Move objects by drag-and-drop or arrows.

Use object diagrams together with class diagrams to validate real scenarios, names, and value consistency.

state.label: State Machine
state.summary: Capture dynamic behavior with states, transitions, and actions.

about.title: About State Machine Diagrams
about.body: State machine diagrams describe behavior changes over time in response to events and conditions.

initialFinal.title: Add Initial And Final Flow
initialFinal.body: Start with an initial node and connect it to the first state.
initialFinal.alt: State machine initial and final states

editState.title: Edit State
editState.body: Double-click a state to update its name, Body, and optional Fallback behavior.

codeBlock.title: Link Code Block
codeBlock.body: Link code behavior by providing function names in state body/fallback fields for precise execution mapping.

bestPractices.title: Best Practices
bestPractices.body: Keep state names explicit, guard transitions properly, and verify that all relevant event paths are modeled.

agent.label: Agent Diagram
agent.summary: Model BAF conversational agents with states, intents, and transition logic.

about.title: Modeling BAF Agents
about.body: Agent diagrams follow a state-machine style where each state has a behavior body and transitions define routing.

addState.title: Add Agent State
addState.body: Drag an agent state from the palette to the canvas.

editBody.title: Edit Agent State Body
editBody.body:
Double-click an agent state to configure behavior.

  • Text reply: predefined response message.
  • LLM reply: delegate response generation to an LLM.
  • RAG reply: answer using a retrieval-augmented knowledge source.
  • Python code: execute custom behavior logic.

addTransition.title: Add Transition Between States
addTransition.body: Drag from the outer part of a source state to a target state to define a transition.

transitionCondition.title: Set Transition Condition
transitionCondition.body:
Double-click a transition and configure condition rules such as:

  • When Intent Matched
  • When No Intent Matched
  • Variable Operation Matched
  • File Received
  • Auto Transition

initialState.title: Set Initial State
initialState.body: Connect the initial node to the state where the conversation should begin.

defineIntents.title: Define Intents
defineIntents.body: Add intent elements and define intent names plus training sentences to improve recognition quality. Intent descriptions help clarify the meaning and purpose of each intent.

customization.title: Agent Customization
customization.body:
Open Agent Config from the sidebar to configure model and runtime settings for generated agents.

  • Classical intent recognition: train a local model from defined intents.
  • LLM-based intent recognition: delegate intent classification to an LLM.

gui.label: GUI Editor
gui.summary: Build UI screens visually and generate web application frontends.

coreWorkflow.title: Core Workflow
coreWorkflow.body:
Use template blocks, compose layouts, then bind model-based data and actions.

Keep pages modular so generated output remains predictable and maintainable.

quantum.label: Quantum Editor
quantum.summary: Design circuits, configure gates, and generate Qiskit-compatible artifacts.

coreWorkflow.title: Core Workflow
coreWorkflow.body:
Place gates on qubit lines, validate structure, then generate with selected backend settings.

Use shot count and backend selection in Generate for reproducible results.

nn.label: Neural Network
nn.summary: Design layered neural networks, attach datasets and training configuration, and generate PyTorch or TensorFlow code.

coreWorkflow.title: Core Workflow
coreWorkflow.body:
Build a neural network by dropping an NNContainer onto the canvas. Drag layers and TensorOps inside it, then connect them with NNNext relationships to define the forward pass.

Configuration and Training/Test Datasets are optional elements that hold training hyperparameters and dataset metadata. When the diagram is ready, generate PyTorch or TensorFlow code from the Generate menu.

containerLayers.title: Add NN Container, Layers, And TensorOps
containerLayers.body:
Start by dragging an NNContainer from the palette onto the canvas; all neural network modules must live inside it.

Available layers: Conv1D, Conv2D, Conv3D, Pooling, Linear, Flatten, Embedding, Dropout, RNN, LSTM, GRU, LayerNormalization, BatchNormalization. Available TensorOps: reshape, concatenate, transpose, permute, multiply, matmultiply.
containerLayers.alt: NN palette with a dropped layer

connect.title: Connect Modules (NNNext)
connect.body: Drag from a blue connection point on a source module to any target module to create an NNNext relationship. The resulting "next" arrow defines the order of the forward pass regardless of whether the connected modules are layers, TensorOps, or a mix of both.
connect.alt: Two modules connected with an NNNext arrow

editAttributes.title: Edit Module Attributes
editAttributes.body:
Double-click any layer or TensorOp to open its attribute popup. Mandatory attributes are always shown; optional ones are enabled via checkboxes.

Many fields use dropdowns: pooling_type (max, average, adaptive_max, adaptive_average, global_max, global_average), actv_func (relu, leaky_relu, sigmoid, softmax, tanh), tns_type (reshape, concatenate, transpose, permute, multiply, matmultiply), padding_type (valid, same).

List-typed attributes adapt to the module's dimension. A Pooling layer with dimension = 2D expects kernel_dim = [3, 3], while dimension = 3D expects [3, 3, 3]. The same rule applies to stride_dim and output_dim. For TensorOps, the selected tns_type controls which dimension attribute is shown (for example reshape_dim for reshape, concatenate_dim for concatenate).

datasets.title: Datasets (Training And Test)
datasets.body:
Datasets are optional. Drop a Training Dataset and a Test Dataset to declare data sources for the network.

Mandatory attributes are name and path_data (file or folder path to the dataset). Optional attributes are task_type (binary, multi_class, regression) and input_format (csv, images). When input_format = images, two additional attributes appear: shape (for example [32, 32, 3]) and normalize (true or false).

Connect each dataset to the NNContainer with an association line.

configuration.title: Configuration
configuration.body:
Configuration is optional. Drag a Configuration element and connect it to the NNContainer with a composition relationship to set training hyperparameters.

Mandatory attributes: batch_size, epochs, learning_rate, optimizer (sgd, adam, adamW, adagrad), loss_function (crossentropy, binary_crossentropy, mse), and metrics (multi-select from accuracy, precision, recall, f1-score, mae). Optional attributes: weight_decay and momentum.

reference.title: Reference Another Network (NNReference)
reference.body: Use an NNReference element to reuse an NN already defined on the same canvas. Select the target NNContainer from the popup; the referenced network is included as a sub-network during code generation.

validateGenerate.title: Validate And Generate
validateGenerate.body:
Run Quality Check from the top bar to catch structural issues such as disconnected layers or missing mandatory attributes before generating code.

Open the Generate menu and choose a framework and style:

  • PyTorch / Subclassing: torch.nn.Module subclass with an explicit forward pass.
  • PyTorch / Sequential: nn.Sequential composition for strictly sequential architectures.
  • TensorFlow / Subclassing: tf.keras.Model subclass with a custom call().
  • TensorFlow / Sequential: keras.Sequential composition.

NN architecture definition is generated in the selected framework, along with training and evaluation code when datasets and Configuration are defined.

quantum.gateNamePlaceholder: Enter gate name (e.g., Bell State, QFT)

gateDescriptions.H: Hadamard Gate: Creates superposition by rotating the qubit state 180° around the X+Z axis. Transforms |0⟩ to |+⟩ and |1⟩ to |−⟩.
gateDescriptions.X: Pauli-X Gate (NOT): Flips the qubit state. Rotates 180° around the X-axis. Transforms |0⟩ ↔ |1⟩.
gateDescriptions.Y: Pauli-Y Gate: Rotates 180° around the Y-axis. Transforms |0⟩ to i|1⟩ and |1⟩ to -i|0⟩.
gateDescriptions.Z: Pauli-Z Gate (Phase Flip): Rotates 180° around the Z-axis. Leaves |0⟩ unchanged, transforms |1⟩ to -|1⟩.
gateDescriptions.Z^½: S Gate (√Z): Rotates 90° around Z-axis. Adds a phase of i to |1⟩. Two S gates = one Z gate.
gateDescriptions.S_DAG: S-Dagger Gate (inverse √Z): Rotates -90° around Z-axis. Adds a phase of -i to |1⟩. Undoes S gate.
gateDescriptions.X^½: V Gate (√X): Rotates 90° around X-axis. Two V gates = one X (NOT) gate.
gateDescriptions.V_DAG: V-Dagger Gate (inverse √X): Rotates -90° around X-axis. Undoes V gate.
gateDescriptions.SQRT_Y: √Y Gate: Rotates 90° around Y-axis. Two √Y gates = one Y gate.
gateDescriptions.SQRT_Y_DAG: √Y-Dagger Gate (inverse √Y): Rotates -90° around Y-axis. Undoes √Y gate.
gateDescriptions.T: T Gate (⁴√Z): Rotates 45° around Z-axis. Adds π/4 phase to |1⟩. Essential for universal quantum computing.
gateDescriptions.T_DAG: T-Dagger Gate (inverse ⁴√Z): Rotates -45° around Z-axis. Removes π/4 phase. Undoes T gate.
gateDescriptions.SQRT_SQRT_X: ⁴√X Gate: Rotates 45° around X-axis. Four applications = one X (NOT) gate.
gateDescriptions.SQRT_SQRT_X_DAG: ⁴√X-Dagger Gate: Rotates -45° around X-axis. Undoes X^¼ gate.
gateDescriptions.SQRT_SQRT_Y: ⁴√Y Gate: Rotates 45° around Y-axis. Four applications = one Y gate.
gateDescriptions.SQRT_SQRT_Y_DAG: ⁴√Y-Dagger Gate: Rotates -45° around Y-axis. Undoes Y^¼ gate.
gateDescriptions.SWAP: SWAP Gate: Exchanges the states of two qubits. |01⟩ ↔ |10⟩, while |00⟩ and |11⟩ unchanged.
gateDescriptions.MEASURE: Measurement (Z-basis): Collapses qubit superposition to |0⟩ or |1⟩. Result is probabilistic based on qubit amplitudes.
gateDescriptions.MEASURE_X: Measurement (X-basis): Collapses qubit to |+⟩ or |−⟩. Equivalent to H then Z-measurement then H.
gateDescriptions.MEASURE_Y: Measurement (Y-basis): Collapses qubit to |i⟩ or |−i⟩. Measures phase relative to Y-axis.
gateDescriptions.CONTROL: Control: Conditions other gates on this qubit being |1⟩. Creates CNOT, Toffoli, and other controlled gates.
gateDescriptions.ANTI_CONTROL: Anti-Control: Conditions other gates on this qubit being |0⟩. Opposite of regular control.
gateDescriptions.POST_SELECT_OFF: Post-Select |0⟩: Forces qubit to |0⟩. Discards branches where qubit would be |1⟩.
gateDescriptions.POST_SELECT_ON: Post-Select |1⟩: Forces qubit to |1⟩. Discards branches where qubit would be |0⟩.
gateDescriptions.POST_SELECT_Y_OFF: Post-Select |i⟩: Forces qubit to Y+ eigenstate (|0⟩+i|1⟩)/√2.
gateDescriptions.POST_SELECT_Y_ON: Post-Select |−i⟩: Forces qubit to Y− eigenstate (|0⟩−i|1⟩)/√2.
gateDescriptions.CONTROL_X: X-Axis Control: Conditions on X-basis (|+⟩/|−⟩) instead of Z-basis (|0⟩/|1⟩).
gateDescriptions.CONTROL_Y: Y-Axis Control: Conditions on Y-basis (|i⟩/|−i⟩) instead of Z-basis.
gateDescriptions.X_POW: X-Rotation (X^t): Rotates by t×180° around X-axis. t=1 is X gate, t=0.5 is √X.
gateDescriptions.Y_POW: Y-Rotation (Y^t): Rotates by t×180° around Y-axis. t=1 is Y gate, t=0.5 is √Y.
gateDescriptions.Z_POW: Z-Rotation (Z^t): Adds t×180° phase to |1⟩. t=1 is Z, t=0.5 is S, t=0.25 is T.
gateDescriptions.EXP_X: X Exponential: e^(-iXt) - rotates around X by angle 2t. Natural form for Hamiltonian simulation.
gateDescriptions.EXP_Y: Y Exponential: e^(-iYt) - rotates around Y by angle 2t. Real-valued rotation matrix.
gateDescriptions.EXP_Z: Z Exponential: e^(-iZt) - phase rotation by angle 2t. Diagonal gate for phase manipulation.
gateDescriptions.Z_POW_T: Spinning Z: Continuously rotates around Z as simulation time t progresses. Phase accumulates over time.
gateDescriptions.Z_POW_NEG_T: Reverse Spinning Z: Rotates backwards around Z axis. Undoes Z^t for time-reversal.
gateDescriptions.Y_POW_T: Spinning Y: Continuously rotates around Y as simulation time progresses.
gateDescriptions.Y_POW_NEG_T: Reverse Spinning Y: Rotates backwards around Y axis as time progresses.
gateDescriptions.X_POW_T: Spinning X: Continuously rotates around X as simulation time progresses.
gateDescriptions.X_POW_NEG_T: Reverse Spinning X: Rotates backwards around X axis as time progresses.
gateDescriptions.Z_FUNC_T: Formulaic Z: Rotation angle is computed from custom function f(t). For complex dynamics.
gateDescriptions.RZ_FUNC_T: Formulaic Rz: Z-axis rotation by f(t) radians. Alternative parametrization of Z rotation.
gateDescriptions.Y_FUNC_T: Formulaic Y: Y-rotation angle from custom function f(t). For complex dynamics.
gateDescriptions.RY_FUNC_T: Formulaic Ry: Y-axis rotation by f(t) radians. Alternative parametrization.
gateDescriptions.X_FUNC_T: Formulaic X: X-rotation angle from custom function f(t). For complex dynamics.
gateDescriptions.RX_FUNC_T: Formulaic Rx: X-axis rotation by f(t) radians. Alternative parametrization.
gateDescriptions.TIME_SHIFT: Time Shift +1: Advances the time parameter for subsequent gates. Used for time-based simulations.
gateDescriptions.TIME_SHIFT_INV: Time Shift -1: Reverses time parameter for subsequent gates. Undoes time advancement.
gateDescriptions.QFT: Quantum Fourier Transform: Converts computational basis to frequency basis. Essential for Shor's algorithm and phase estimation.
gateDescriptions.QFT_DAG: Inverse QFT: Converts frequency basis back to computational basis. Undoes QFT.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_GRADIENT: Phase Gradient: Applies increasing phases across basis states. Used in QFT and phase kickback.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_GRADIENT_DAG: Inverse Phase Gradient: Removes phases applied by Grad. Undoes phase gradient.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_GRADIENT_INV: Inverted Phase Gradient: Applies decreasing phases across basis states.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_GRADIENT_INV_DAG: Inverted Phase Gradient Dagger: Conjugate transpose of Grad⁻¹.
gateDescriptions.INC: Increment: Adds 1 to the quantum register interpreted as a binary number. |n⟩ → |n+1⟩.
gateDescriptions.DEC: Decrement: Subtracts 1 from the quantum register. |n⟩ → |n-1⟩ (wraps around).
gateDescriptions.ADD: Quantum Addition: Adds input register A to target register. Used in quantum arithmetic circuits.
gateDescriptions.SUB: Quantum Subtraction: Subtracts input register A from target. Inverse of addition.
gateDescriptions.MUL: Quantum Multiplication: Multiplies target register by input A. Key for Shor's algorithm.
gateDescriptions.ADD_AB: Add Product: Adds the product A×B to the target register. Multi-register operation.
gateDescriptions.SUB_AB: Subtract Product: Subtracts the product A×B from target. Inverse of +AB.
gateDescriptions.MUL_INV: Inverse Multiplication: Divides by A (multiplies by modular inverse). Undoes ×A.
gateDescriptions.MOD_ADD: Modular Add: Adds A to register mod R. Result wraps around at R. Key for Shor's algorithm.
gateDescriptions.MOD_SUB: Modular Subtract: Subtracts A from register mod R. Inverse of modular addition.
gateDescriptions.MOD_MUL: Modular Multiply: Multiplies register by A mod R. Core of modular exponentiation.
gateDescriptions.MOD_INV_MUL: Modular Division: Multiplies by A⁻¹ mod R. Undoes modular multiplication.
gateDescriptions.MOD_INC: Modular Increment: Adds 1 to register mod R. Wraps R-1 to 0.
gateDescriptions.MOD_DEC: Modular Decrement: Subtracts 1 from register mod R. Wraps 0 to R-1.
gateDescriptions.MOD_MUL_B: Modular Multiply by B: Multiplies by second input B mod R. Multi-register operation.
gateDescriptions.MOD_MUL_B_INV: Modular Multiply B by A-inverse: Computes B×A⁻¹ mod R. For reversible computation.
gateDescriptions.COMPARE: Less Than Comparison: Sets output qubit to |1⟩ if A < B. Quantum comparison circuit.
gateDescriptions.GREATER_THAN: Greater Than Comparison: Sets output to |1⟩ if register A > register B.
gateDescriptions.LESS_EQUAL: Less or Equal: Sets output to |1⟩ if register A ≤ register B.
gateDescriptions.GREATER_EQUAL: Greater or Equal: Sets output to |1⟩ if register A ≥ register B.
gateDescriptions.EQUAL: Equality Test: Sets output to |1⟩ if registers A and B have same value.
gateDescriptions.NOT_EQUAL: Inequality Test: Sets output to |1⟩ if registers A and B differ.
gateDescriptions.COMPARE_A_LT: Compare to Input A: Sets output to |1⟩ if qubit register < input A value.
gateDescriptions.COMPARE_A_GT: Compare to Input A: Sets output to |1⟩ if qubit register > input A value.
gateDescriptions.COMPARE_A_EQ: Compare to Input A: Sets output to |1⟩ if qubit register equals input A value.
gateDescriptions.COUNT_1S: Population Count: Counts the number of |1⟩ qubits in the register. Output is binary representation.
gateDescriptions.CYCLE_BITS: Cycle Bits: Rotates qubit positions cyclically. Top qubit moves to bottom, others shift up.
gateDescriptions.XOR: XOR Parity: Computes XOR of all qubits in register. Output |1⟩ if odd number of |1⟩s.
gateDescriptions.INPUT_A: Input A: Initializes qubits to classical value A (adjustable). Creates computational basis state |A⟩.
gateDescriptions.INPUT_B: Input B: Initializes qubits to classical value B (adjustable). Second input for arithmetic operations.
gateDescriptions.RANDOM: Random State: Initializes qubit to random point on Bloch sphere. Creates mixed state for testing.
gateDescriptions.INPUT_R: Input R (Modulus): Sets the modulus value for modular arithmetic operations.
gateDescriptions.MYSTERY: Mystery Gate: A random unitary gate. Different each time - useful for testing and games.
gateDescriptions.ZERO: Zero Projection: Projects onto |0⟩ state. Non-unitary operation that destroys information.
gateDescriptions.UNIVERSAL_NOT: Universal NOT: Anti-unitary operation that flips any qubit state to its orthogonal. Impossible to build physically.
gateDescriptions.ONE: Identity Gate: Does nothing to the qubit. Useful as placeholder or for circuit clarity.
gateDescriptions.MINUS_ONE: Global Phase (-1): Multiplies entire state by -1. Unobservable but matters in interference.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_I: Global Phase (i): Rotates global phase by 90°. Multiplies state by imaginary unit i.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_MINUS_I: Global Phase (-i): Rotates global phase by -90°. Multiplies state by -i.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_SQRT_I: Global Phase (√i): Rotates global phase by 45°. Two applications give phase i.
gateDescriptions.PHASE_SQRT_MINUS_I: Global Phase (√-i): Rotates global phase by -45°. Two applications give phase -i.
gateDescriptions.BLOCH: Bloch Sphere: Visualizes single qubit state on unit sphere. Poles are |0⟩/|1⟩, equator is superpositions.
gateDescriptions.DENSITY: Density Matrix (ρ): Shows full quantum state including mixed states. Diagonal = probabilities, off-diagonal = coherences.
gateDescriptions.AMPLITUDE: Amplitude Display: Shows complex amplitudes for each basis state. Height = magnitude, angle = phase.
gateDescriptions.CHANCE: Chance Display: Shows probability (0-100%) of measuring |1⟩ for this qubit.
gateDescriptions.INTERLEAVE: Interleave: Shuffles qubits like interleaving two halves of a deck. Useful for QFT optimization.
gateDescriptions.DEINTERLEAVE: Deinterleave: Undoes interleave operation. Separates alternating qubits back into halves.
gateDescriptions.REVERSE_BITS: Reverse Bits: Flips the order of qubits. Often needed after QFT to correct bit ordering.
gateDescriptions.ROTATE_BITS_LEFT: Rotate Left: Cyclically shifts all qubits up by one position. Top wraps to bottom.
gateDescriptions.ROTATE_BITS_RIGHT: Rotate Right: Cyclically shifts all qubits down by one position. Bottom wraps to top.
gateDescriptions.SAMPLE: Sample: Takes a probabilistic sample of qubit state without full collapse. For statistical analysis.
gateDescriptions.DETECT: Detect: Simulates physical detector response. Models realistic measurement imperfections.
gateDescriptions.AXIS_SAMPLE: 3-Axis Sample: Samples qubit in X, Y, and Z bases simultaneously. For tomographic reconstruction.
